text:
- chief complaint: right ankle pain after a fall on ice, with a popping sensation at the time of injury.
- history of present illness: the patient slipped on ice while taking out the trash and felt a pop. Initially unable to bear weight and needed help getting indoors; now bearing a little weight with a limp. Pain was severe at first, now about 6/10, constant and throbbing. Ice, elevation, and ibuprofen have provided little relief. No prior injury to this ankle.
- physical examination: vitals normal (BP 120/80, SpO2 98%). Right ankle shows lateral malleolus ecchymosis and swelling, tenderness over the anterior lateral soft tissue, no laxity on anterior drawer or inversion stress, no bony tenderness of the foot. Neurovascular exam intact (capillary refill under 3 seconds, dorsalis pedis pulse strong, sensation intact). X-ray showed no fracture.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: pain (throbbing, constant, about 6/10), warmth, swelling, bruising, limping, difficulty bearing weight. No numbness or tingling.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: N/A.
- follow-up instructions: diagnosis of right ankle sprain. Keep leg elevated, ice five times daily for 20 minutes, use an air cast, and use crutches and avoid weight-bearing for 1–2 days, then walk as tolerated. Expect recovery in 2–3 weeks. Return to the office if pain persists after this week, with possible MRI.
